title: One-step simulation of the controller
statement: Let $D$, $M_1$, and $M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration of $D$ on an input $x$ whose state is not the halting state. Then one step of the conditional-dispatch machine, started from the configuration encoding $c$, is the encoding of the configuration reached by taking one step of $D$ from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a configuration of $D$ on input $x$
The state of $c$ is not the halting state
replaced:
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet and let $c$ be a
configuration of $D$ on an input $x$ whose state is not the halting state.
Then one step of the conditional-dispatch machine from the embedded controller
configuration of $c$ equals the embedded controller configuration of one step
of $D$ from $c$; in particular the register tracks the first symbol of the
simulated output, with no hypothesis on $c$'s output.
